labels.label: bzdef:c2s2d6_pseudo_boule

hypotheses.paper: V une variété localement projective, M ∈ V
hypotheses.note: [ChartedSpace (S n) V] for the definition; [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] in the theorems that use it

r : ℝ arbitrary, an extension of Déf. 6, whose radii are r > 0 in the paper's usage (r ≥ 0 under Bourbaki's convention; question under Prop. 5). For r ≤ 0 the Lean pseudo-ball is empty (pseudoBoule_eq_empty_of_nonpos). On Déf. 6's radii, under either reading, the definition is the paper's.

hypotheses.paper: il existe au moins un segment fermé d'extrémités M, N, majoré par r
hypotheses.note: ∃ Sg, IsMajoreSeg n r Sg M N: a closed segment of V (Déf. 14) from M to N, majorised by r in V (Déf. 2, Mesure). The order of the endpoints is immaterial (mem_pseudoBoule_comm, via IsMajoreSeg.symm). Equivalently ∃ Sg segment with pseudoLength n Sg M N < r (mem_pseudoBoule_iff)

findings: Unlabelled sentence after Déf. 6 (l.417–418), « La pseudo-boule … est un ouvert connexe (cf. 3°, 5°) ». The statement holds in every dimension and for every r (pseudoBoule_ouvert_connexe), with « connexe » read as in the question below. The justification « cf. 5° » leaves one step implicit. 5° bounds the pseudo-length of segments near (M, N), but it does not produce a segment from M to each point N′ near N, and openness needs one. The formalized proof gets it from the chart of a segment majorising (M, N), with the estimate behind 5° (eventually_exists_projMeasure_lt, in isOpen_pseudoBoule). Connectedness follows 3° as printed: each pseudo-ball is the union of majorised segments from its centre, by sub-segments and pseudoLength_mono.

Unlabelled sentence after Déf. 6 (l.420–423, [sic] « lcs »), « il résulte du 6° que les pseudo-boules … forment une base de voisinages ». 6° by itself does not give this. Continuity, and vanishing exactly on the diagonal, do not make small balls small: a continuous function vanishing only at M may tend to 0 far from M. The formalized proof (hasBasis_pseudoBoule) adds two facts. The pseudo-balls are connected (the preceding sentence), and V is locally compact. Then l_V(M, ·) ≥ r > 0 on the frontier of a compact neighbourhood C, and the connected ball B(M, r) contains M and misses that frontier, so it lies in C. The statement is unaffected for n ≥ 1.

The neighbourhood-basis sentence (l.420–423) fails in dimension 0. {x} is a convex body of S(0), and its pseudo-balls are empty (pseudoBoule_dim_zero), so they are not neighbourhoods. BaseVoisinagesPrinted n holds iff 0 < n (baseVoisinagesPrinted_iff). This is OQ-45: under (b), a point given measure 0, the balls of radius r > 0 would be {x} and the sentence would hold. OQ-56 does not bear on it.
questions: « un ouvert connexe » (l.417). Reading taken: Bourbaki's definition, not the union of two disjoint non-empty open sets. Under it the empty set is connected; Lean IsPreconnected. The sentence then holds in every dimension and for every r (pseudoBoule_ouvert_connexe). Under the reading « non-empty and connected » (Lean IsConnected), it holds for every Déf. 6 radius r > 0 when n ≥ 1 (isConnected_pseudoBoule_iff). It fails only at n = 0 (OQ-45), and at r = 0 if « positif » includes 0. Both forms are proved, so the Lean is at least the paper under either reading, and the reading matters only in dimension 0.

« de rayon quelconque » (l.422). Reading taken: all radii r > 0. In the paper's usage these are exactly Déf. 6's radii. If « positif » included 0, the reading would drop only r = 0, whose ball ∅ is no neighbourhood, so the sentence could not hold otherwise. The Lean form is (𝓝 M).HasBasis (fun r => 0 < r) (pseudoBoule n M).

« Si V est l'intérieur d'un corps convexe » (l.420). Reading taken: V = corpsInterior K for a convex body K of S(n) (IsCorpsConvexeS n K), with its induced structure, as in Prop. 2 (Benzecri.Chapter2.Hilbert).

labels.label: bzprop:c2s2p5_ouvert_plein

hypotheses.paper: V une variété localement projective connexe
hypotheses.note: [TopologicalSpace V] [ChartedSpace (S n) V] [HasGroupoid V (projGroupoid n)] [PreconnectedSpace V], V in any universe. U non-empty makes V non-empty. Hausdorff and second countability are never used

hypotheses.paper: U un ouvert non vide de V
hypotheses.note: hU : IsOpen U, hne : U.Nonempty in ouvert_plein. eq_univ_of_forall_pseudoBoule_subset drops IsOpen U (weakened), since openness follows

hypotheses.paper: r un nombre réel (the radius of « la pseudo-boule de centre M et de rayon r »)
hypotheses.note: 0 < r: r is a Déf. 6 radius, « un nombre réel positif », read > 0 as in the paper's usage (question). If « positif » includes 0, the case r = 0 fails (ouvert_plein_counterexample). Negative radii are outside Déf. 6 under either reading.

hypotheses.paper: quel que soit M ∈ U, la pseudo-boule de centre M et de rayon r est incluse dans U
hypotheses.note: ∀ M ∈ U, pseudoBoule n M r ⊆ U
every n: for n = 0 a manifold charted on S(0) is discrete (discreteTopology_dim_zero), so a connected V is at most a point (subsingleton_dim_zero)

findings: Once r > 0, the hypothesis « U ouvert » of Prop. 5 (l.426) is redundant. U contains the pseudo-ball of each of its points, and for n ≥ 1 a pseudo-ball of radius r > 0 is open and contains its centre (isOpen_of_forall_pseudoBoule_subset). In dimension 0 a connected V is a point (subsingleton_dim_zero). eq_univ_of_forall_pseudoBoule_subset proves Prop. 5 without this hypothesis.
questions: Does « positif » mean > 0 in Déf. 6 (« r un nombre réel positif », l.412), and so for Prop. 5's radius (l.426, « r un nombre réel », the radius of « la pseudo-boule de centre M et de rayon r »)? Reading taken: > 0, the paper's usage. Under it Benzecri.ouvert_plein is Prop. 5 as printed, in every dimension, and its printed broken-line proof (Prop. 4, k > 0) agrees. The row is left partial and unmarked pending the ruling. If the ruling is > 0, the mark goes on Benzecri.ouvert_plein with no Lean change. If « positif » includes 0 (Bourbaki), the case r = 0 fails in every dimension n ≥ 1. The witness is S(n) ∖ {x} in the connected S(n): every pseudo-ball of radius 0 is empty (ouvert_plein_counterexample). OuvertPleinPrinted n, which extends pseudoBoule to every real radius, holds iff n = 0 (ouvertPleinPrinted_iff). That is the paper only through r = 0, and only under ≥ 0. Evidence that the paper's usage reads « positif » as > 0. Ch. 1 Déf. 3 (ch1 l.168–169) calls « le groupe multiplicatif ℝ⁺ » the group of « homothéties positives », and ch1 l.527 calls it « le groupe ℝ⁺ des réels positifs »; both must be ]0, ∞[. The open hemisphere has F(H) = l⁻¹(ℝ⁺) (ch1 l.205), read 0 < l v by Sphere.openHemisphere. Ch. 2 l.82 writes « positif ou nul ». At ch2 l.669, « Soit k un nombre réel positif » with ma/ab < k forces k > 0. « strictement positif » also occurs (ch2 l.366, 383, 470), so the usage is not uniform, but no occurrence of « positif » includes 0.

kb_proposals: Pseudo-balls (Déf. 6) are Benzecri.pseudoBoule (BenzecriScaffold.Chapter2.PseudoBoules). They are open (isOpen_pseudoBoule) and preconnected (isPreconnected_pseudoBoule) in every dimension and for every r. IsMajoreSeg n k Sg M N ↔ pseudoLength n Sg M N < k (isMajoreSeg_iff_pseudoLength_lt). Sub-segments: IsProjSegment.exists_subset_left. Reversal: IsProjSegment.symm, IsMajoreSeg.symm. In the interior of a convex body the pseudo-ball is the hilbertLength ball (mem_pseudoBoule_corpsInterior_iff).

A manifold charted on S(0) is discrete (discreteTopology_dim_zero), so a connected one has at most one point (subsingleton_dim_zero). Use these for the dimension-0 case of any statement about a connected V.

S(n) is connected for n ≥ 1 (connectedSpace_S, via S.homeomorphEuclideanSphere and Mathlib's isConnected_sphere), and second countable via (S.homeomorphEuclideanSphere n).secondCountableTopology. That makes S(n) ∖ {x} a cheap witness against a 'connected V' statement that is printed as true.

Do not elaborate (continuous_hilbertLength hK).comp h against the expected type Continuous fun P => hilbertLength K M P: the isDefEq check times out. Compose in a have, then simp only [Function.comp_def] at it.
